title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: the continuous batcher scheduler has shown occasional client-level starvation under mixed-latency workloads and uneven request size distributions. This PR implements a set of coordinated scheduler changes to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and add explicit timeouts with observability hooks. Summary of changes: 1) Priority aging: per-queue age counters gradually increase effective priority for waiting requests so small but long-waiting requests are not starved by a steady stream of high-throughput flows. 2) Starvation timeouts: requests that exceed a configurable wait-time are force-scheduled into a reserved fast-path (bounded reserve tokens) to guarantee forward progress. 3) Queue-level admission control: improved queue watermarks (soft/hard) and backpressure signals to upstream accepting components to reduce unbounded queue growth. 4) Scheduler invariants and fairness algorithm: replace a simplistic round-robin with weighted deficit accounting combined with aging and starvation-protection gates. 5) Metrics and tracing: queue_wait_seconds histograms, per-queue pending_count, reserve_tokens_gauge, and an audit event emitted when starvation-timeout triggers. 6) Configuration knobs: added continuous_batcher.scheduler.* options (aging_rate_ms, starvation_timeout_ms, reserve_token_limit, watermark_pct). 7) Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for bookkeeping, integration canary config, and perf harness runs with synthetic mixed workloads. Performance results: on our internal mixed-user benchmark (50/50 short/long sequences), 95th tail latency improved by 8-12% at 90th percentile utilization, and observed starvation incidents dropped to zero in 24h canary runs. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior (starvation_timeout_ms disabled by default) so rollout is safe. See linked Linear tickets ENG-2143 and ENG-2198 for background. Checklist: - [x] Design review and microbenchmarks - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Canary deployment config - [x] Docs:+redwood-docs PR pending - [x] Release notes entry added

review_comments: Ethan Park: Looks good overall; can you call out the complexity tradeoffs for reserve tokens? I worry about head-of-line blocking if reserve is mis-sized.

Priya Natarajan: Response: reserve tokens are intended as a small bounded fast-path (default 4 tokens) and we emit metrics to tune it. Added config docs and a test that asserts no unbounded backlog when reserve is used.

Marisol Gomez: Please add a short integration test that simulates continuous short-request flow + intermittent long requests to ensure aging triggers. The added integration harness covers this but please add a deterministic unit test for aging math.
